title: Against Vorstius on eternity; rules 1-3
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Vorstius Conrad unto this doctrine contradicts in Notes belonging toward Disputation III On God page 226, ye common opinion belonging toward eternity existing all at once false unto be contending. Unto that reason certain foundations plus rules here we hand down. 1. Belonging toward God eternity not accident stands as, but substance belonging toward God — for in reality nothing other than duration belonging toward God it stands as, plus duration nothing other than persevering existence. 2. Belonging toward God eternity indivisible plus entirely simultaneous stands as, plus parts succeeding one another has in no wise. 3. Belonging toward God eternity, indivisible being, with all differences belonging toward times necessarily exists — in no wise that all parts belonging toward time together among themselves exist, but that each part belonging toward time, while in act it stands as, with eternity exists.
pass_b_english: Conrad Vorstius contradicts this doctrine in Notes on Disputation III On God p. 226, contending that the common opinion of eternity existing all at once is false. For that reason we hand down certain foundations and rules here.

1. God's eternity is not an accident, but God's substance — for it is in reality nothing other than God's duration, and duration nothing other than persevering existence. 2. God's eternity is indivisible and entirely simultaneous, and has no parts succeeding one another. 3. God's eternity, being indivisible, necessarily exists with all differences of times — not that all parts of time exist together among themselves, but that each part of time, while it is in act, exists with eternity.
source_text: CONTRADICIT huic doctrinae CONR. VORSTIUS Notis ad disp. III. de Deo p.226, vulgarem sententiam de aeternitate tota simul existente falsam esse contendens. Quapropter fundamenta et regulas quasdam hic trademus. 1. Aeternitas Dei non est accidens, sed substantia Dei — est enim reipsa nihil aliud quam duratio Dei, et duratio nihil aliud quam existentia durans. 2. Aeternitas Dei est indivisibilis et tota simul, neque habet partes sibi invicem succedentes. 3. Aeternitas Dei, cum sit indivisibilis, necessario existit cum omnibus temporum differentiis — non quod omnes partes temporis simul inter se existant, sed quod singulae partes temporis dum actu sunt existunt cum aeternitate.
